title: Exactly One Edit Apart
statement: An **edit** is one of: inserting one letter, deleting one letter, or replacing one letter by a different one. Return `true` if `first` can be turned into `second` with **exactly one** edit, otherwise `false`. Two identical texts need zero edits, so for them the answer is `false`.
constraints: both texts use only lowercase English letters

examples.explanation: The texts are identical: zero edits are needed, not one.

hints.nudge: How different can the lengths be if only one edit happened? And what does the position of the first difference tell you?
hints.pattern: Compare from the front until the first mismatch, then compare the REST of the texts in the way the edit type requires.
hints.walkthrough: Computing the full edit distance with a table works but costs O(n * m). One edit means the texts are almost the same. First the lengths: if they differ by more than 1 the answer is false. Let a be the shorter one. Move along both texts while the letters are equal and stop at the first mismatch i. If you reached the end of a without a mismatch, the texts are equal (false) or b has exactly one extra letter at the end (true). Otherwise decide by the lengths: with equal lengths the mismatching letters must be a replacement, so everything after position i must be equal; with different lengths b has an extra letter at position i, so a[i:] must equal b[i+1:]. One pass: O(n).
